posts.content: Track actions; cooperate when the opponent is likely good and cooperative, defect when selfishness or defection is likely. Optimize good-player aggregate payoffs.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.

As a good player, prioritize total payoff of good players: cooperate absent evidence, since mutual cooperation benefits both good players. Reassess from encounter outcomes; selfish players are likely to defect.
Favor cooperation with likely-good players; use observed actions to update beliefs and defect against likely-selfish opponents.
Prioritize payoff: defect by default, but use observed opponent behavior to identify reliable cooperators; reciprocate only when expected to outperform defection.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff; defect against likely selfish players. Use observed actions to update beliefs, and remember there are no repeat encounters.
Play D every round; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.

Against likely good players, cooperate to preserve mutual gains. A selfish player should defect, so use observed encounter behavior to identify and defect against likely selfish opponents; reassess as evidence accumulates.

As good, maximize total good-player payoff: cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions and reciprocate defections when the opponent seems good.
As a good player, favor C with likely-good opponents and D with likely-selfish ones; update beliefs from actual encounter outcomes, treating claims cautiously.

For each encounter, cooperate with likely-good partners to maximize their combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish partners or those who defect, since selfish payoffs are excluded. Use observed behavior to update beliefs and reciprocate where future meetings remain possible.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate absent strong evidence the opponent is selfish; defect when the chance they are selfish exceeds roughly one half. Treat observed defections as evidence, but not proof.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when evidence makes selfishness likely. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. P7’s defection is evidence they may be selfish, but it’s only one observation.
Continue defecting every round; against either opponent action, D yields at least as much as C, and more when they cooperate.

Good-player objective: cooperate with likely-good cooperators; defect against likely-selfish players or likely defectors. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions; past cooperation is evidence, not proof.
I’ll cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones, and update beliefs using observed actions.

P7’s defection raises suspicion, but one observation is weak evidence. With no communication, cooperate when mutual cooperation is likely among good players; defect when expected to protect good-player payoffs against selfishness or likely defection. Update cautiously from encounters.
Defect: D strictly dominates C against either opponent action.
As a good player, cooperate with an untested opponent; defect only when evidence makes them more likely selfish than good. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P7 absent evidence of selfishness; prioritize joint payoff among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions and defect when the opponent is likely selfish.
Defect this round and throughout: each opponent is met only once, so defection maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Assume selfish players defect. Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is more likely. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Continue choosing D each round; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to preserve mutual gains; defect when the opponent is likely selfish, since against their defection it improves my payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents: mutual cooperation benefits both good players. Defect when the opponent is likely selfish or persistently defects; update beliefs from observed play.
P6 is unobserved. As a good player, favor C with a likely-good opponent and D when selfish play is likely; update from actual actions.

P7 and P2 defected against my cooperation, making future defection against likely defectors prudent. P9 cooperated. With no communication, use the prior and observed play; cooperate when mutual cooperation among good players is likely, otherwise protect the good-player total.
Defect this round: it yields more than cooperation against either opponent action.
Cooperate with untested P4; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Continue treating P5’s defection as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs from observed actions.
P7's defection is evidence of selfishness, but not proof. Cooperate with untested players; against likely selfish opponents, defect to protect good players' payoffs.
Defect each round: it strictly dominates cooperation against either opponent action. Encounters are one-off, so reputation or reciprocity cannot improve my payoff.

Against a good player, C maximizes combined good-player payoff; against a selfish player, D protects my payoff. Selfish players have a strict incentive to D, so update cautiously from observed defections.
Defect every round; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with plausible good opponents; defect when evidence strongly suggests selfishness. For untested opponents, weigh mutual gains against the chance they are selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player total; against likely selfish players, defect to avoid giving them gains and protect my payoff. Update beliefs from observed play.

Continue cooperating with known-good players. Against an unknown opponent, cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness; selfish players defect, so defecting against them protects my own good-player payoff.

Against a likely-good player, cooperate: it maximizes the combined payoff whether they choose C or D. Against a likely-selfish player, defect. Update cautiously from observed actions; no communication.
Defect this round: D strictly dominates C against either opponent action, and there is no future rematch.

Against an untested opponent, cooperate; defect when evidence puts their chance of being selfish above roughly one half. Update from observed actions, remembering good players’ welfare—not selfish players’ payoffs—is the objective.
P7’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness. Cooperate with untested opponents such as P1; against likely selfish players, defect to protect good players’ payoffs.
Defect this round; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P7’s action, and this is a one-time encounter.
Against P9, cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish. A selfish opponent favors D, while mutual cooperation maximizes welfare when both are good.
Continue choosing D; it maximizes my payoff against either action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against strongly suspected selfish players. P2 and P5 defected against my cooperation, so treat them as likely selfish. Reassess after each encounter.
As a good player, favor C with likely-good opponents and D against likely-selfish ones. Prioritize reciprocal cooperation, but update cautiously: observed C is evidence of goodness, not proof.
P4, P6, P8, and P9 cooperated, so treat them as good. Against P2, cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish, since selfish players maximize their own payoff by defecting.
P5 has no observed history; use the prior. Cooperate with likely-good players, defect against likely-selfish players, and update from observed play.
Defect this round: D strictly dominates C against either action, and there is no future rematch.
P2 is untested; cooperate if evidence from observed play makes them likely good. Keep P5’s defection as strong selfishness evidence and account for the limited total number of selfish players.
Cooperate with untested P6 to support good players’ joint payoff; selfish players are likely to defect. Use observed actions to update beliefs and respond accordingly.
For each unplayed pairing, cooperate when the opponent is likely good; defect when selfishness is likely. Treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty, and avoid overinterpreting cooperation.
Defect this round; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize shared gains; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. P2 and P5’s defections are strong evidence; reassess from each new encounter.

Cooperate with P8: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and observed cooperation is evidence of goodness. Reassess after seeing their action; selfish players optimizing their payoff should defect against C.
Against P7, cooperate unless there is evidence they are selfish; defecting against likely selfish players protects good-player welfare. Treat observed actions as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; against likely-selfish opponents, defect to protect the good-player total. Treat observed defection as evidence of selfishness, but update cautiously.
Defect this round: D strictly dominates C regardless of P9’s action.
P5 and P2 defected against my cooperation; retain suspicion, but prioritize good-player welfare. Against P7, cooperate unless strong evidence suggests selfishness.

P5 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence suggests selfishness. Selfish players should defect, so use observed actions to update beliefs and defect against likely-selfish opponents; favor C-C among good players.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time encounter.
P5 and P7 defected against me, strong evidence they are selfish; cooperation by P3, P4, P9, and P10 supports good roles. Against P8, cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish.
Choose D this round; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is plausible; defect against players strongly suspected selfish, who are likely to defect. Update beliefs from observed actions.
P2 is still more likely good than selfish after six observed cooperators; cooperate this round. Continue C with likely-good players, since mutual cooperation maximizes their combined payoff.
P1 is unobserved. Use encounter actions as evidence, not certainty; cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect when selfish play is sufficiently likely to improve good-player welfare.

P2, P5, and P7 defected against my C, consistent with selfishness; P9, P4, P8, and P10 cooperated. For unseen P6, favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness; good-player aggregate is best served by mutual cooperation.
Defect against P4; D yields more than C against either action.
Cooperate with P10: the observed defections identify selfish players, while P10 remains more likely good. Continue updating from exact actions.
P5 and P7’s defections are evidence of selfishness; the others cooperated when tested. Treat untested P2 as likely good and favor cooperation to maximize good players’ combined payoff.
Defect against P9; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P5 and P7’s defections are evidence of selfishness, not certainty. With no repeat encounters, selfish players have a strong incentive to defect. For remaining rounds, weigh that evidence against the welfare gains from mutual cooperation with good players.
Defect against P8; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
With two rounds left, cooperate with untested P7: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and current evidence doesn’t justify suspecting P7 is selfish. Update from the encounter.

P5 is unobserved. Cooperate if they seem good; defect against likely selfish players, who benefit from our cooperation. Prior C behavior supports goodness, while P2’s D is evidence of selfishness but not proof.
P2 and P7’s defections identify them as selfish; the others who cooperated are good. P3 remains uncertain, so cooperate unless new evidence changes the balance.
P3 is unobserved. Cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness highly likely; against a good opponent, C best serves the good-player total even if they defect.
Defect against P6; D gives me a higher payoff than C regardless of their action.
Against untested P1, cooperate to support good-player welfare; defect only with strong evidence they are selfish.
Cooperate with P8 unless strong evidence suggests selfishness; favor mutual cooperation among good players and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect against P10: D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action in this one-time encounter.
P2 is unobserved and likely good; cooperate to maximize good-player welfare. Keep P5/P7 as likely selfish based on their defections, but account for the fixed-count prior.
Continue choosing D each round; it maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with untested opponents to preserve mutual gains among good players; defect only when strong evidence suggests selfishness.
P7 is unobserved. Favor C if they seem likely good; D can protect good-player payoffs against a selfish defector. P2 and P5’s defections are evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
P2 and P7 defected; all other observed players cooperated. Given selfish players strictly prefer D, P5 is the only remaining possible selfish player, so defect against P5.
P5 defected against my C earlier. In this final encounter, defect if P5 is selfish; cooperate if P5 is good, since that maximizes the good-player total.
Defect: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
P10 cooperated when we met, so cooperate again to support good-player welfare. Prior defections by P2, P5, and P7 suggest selfishness but are not conclusive.
P6 cooperated in our earlier encounter, so I regard them as likely good. Favor C-C; defect only if new evidence strongly supports selfishness.
Final round: defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P1’s action.
Against P4, cooperate: their earlier cooperation supports a good role, and mutual cooperation maximizes welfare if both are good.
Final round: choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either action.
Final round against P7, who defected against my cooperation. Defect: this protects good-player payoff if P7 defects again, and limits the loss if P7 is good.
Final round: P2’s earlier defection suggests selfishness, but is not conclusive. Choose to maximize good-player payoff, weighing that evidence against the benefit of mutual cooperation.
P3 cooperated in our earlier encounter, so is good under payoff-maximizing selfish play. Favor C against P3.

belief_records.strategy: Favor cooperation when it improves good players’ combined payoff; adapt to observed actions and defect when doing so better protects the good-player total.
Defect each round: D gives a higher payoff than C against either action, and there is no future rematch.
As a good player, cooperate when there is no evidence an opponent is selfish; reassess from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown players; update selfishness beliefs from observed actions and defect when expected gains to good players favor it.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff; adapt only if observed behavior makes cooperation more profitable.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize total good-player payoffs; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect in each encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff; use encounter evidence to identify selfish players and adapt.
As a good player, cooperate when the expected gains to good players outweigh the risk of helping a selfish opponent; update from observed actions and reciprocate defections when appropriate.
As a good player, cooperate when the expected welfare of good players favors it; defect when facing likely selfish play. Update beliefs from encounter outcomes and treat claims cautiously.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player payoffs; update beliefs from observed behavior and defect when selfishness makes that better for the good-player total.
Defect: D strictly dominates C against either opponent action.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; update beliefs from observed actions and suspect P5 after their defection.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect against likely-selfish players, who should defect. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff; P3’s cooperation against my defection is evidence they are not selfish. Otherwise retain the conditional prior.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize total good-player payoffs; defect against likely selfish players. P7's defection updates my beliefs; no repeat encounters.
Defect: it earns at least as much as cooperation against either opponent action.

Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits both good players; defect against likely selfish players. Treat P2’s defection against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate when facing a likely-good player because cooperation raises total good-player payoff; defect only when the opponent is likely selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to raise good-player welfare; defect when selfish play is likely. P4’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play.
Cooperate when it is likely to raise good players’ combined payoff; update cautiously from observed actions and defect when that better protects the good-player total.
Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either action, with no repeat encounter.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; treat P5’s defection as evidence of selfishness and update as more outcomes are observed.
Cooperate with P7: cooperation yields higher expected payoff for the good players given current identity beliefs. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time encounter. P3’s cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness; retain the conditional prior for others.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. P3’s cooperation suggests good, while P7’s defection suggests selfish.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. Prioritize observed cooperation as evidence that an opponent is not selfish.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to preserve mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior and defect against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with likely-good players when it improves total good-player payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when facing likely selfish players.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to improve good-player welfare; defect when selfish play is likely. P4 and P8 cooperated, so I rule them out as selfish.
Cooperate when it best raises the good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior and defect when that better protects the good-player total.
Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action, and there is no repeat encounter.
Cooperate with untested opponents when selfishness seems below one half; treat P5’s defection as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness, and update from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect against likely selfish opponents. P7’s defection against my cooperation strongly indicates selfishness.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time encounter. P3 and P8 cooperated against my defection, so they are not selfish; retain the conditional prior for others.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. P3 and P10 cooperated, while P7’s defection suggests selfishness.
Choose D each round: it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Prioritize observed actions when updating identity beliefs.
Cooperate with untested opponents to preserve gains among good players; defect only when evidence strongly suggests selfishness. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs. The three observed cooperators are good; update remaining identity beliefs using the conditioned count prior.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. P4, P6, and P8 cooperated, so I rule them out as selfish.
Cooperate when it best increases good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior and defect only when that better protects the good-player total.
Defect: D yields more than C against either action, and this opponent will not be faced again.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation lowers suspicion, while P5’s defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested opponents when that best supports the good players’ joint payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P7’s action in this one-time encounter. Prior cooperation against my defections rules out selfishness for P3, P6, and P8.

Cooperate with P9 absent strong evidence they are selfish; cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when both are good. Observed defections make P5 and P7 likely selfish, while P3 and P10 cooperated.
Choose D to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence the opponent is not selfish; a defection alone is not conclusive.

Cooperate with untested opponents to preserve gains among good players; defect against strongly suspected selfish players. Prior cooperation suggests P1 and P10 are good, while P2 and P5’s defections raise suspicion.

Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize total good-player payoff; defect against likely selfish players. Prior cooperation rules out selfishness under selfish payoff maximization; condition remaining beliefs on those observations.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to raise good-player welfare. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; against an unobserved opponent, cooperate unless selfish play is sufficiently likely.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize their combined payoff; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed behavior and use the prior for unobserved opponents.
Defect: D strictly dominates C, and this opponent will not be faced again.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation lowers suspicion, while P5’s defection remains evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P6, whose selfishness likelihood is low. Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ joint payoff; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; cooperation by P3, P6, and P8 against my defections rules out selfishness. Retain the prior for others.

Cooperate absent strong evidence P4 is selfish: cooperation improves welfare when both players are good. Prior defections by P5 and P7 raise suspicion, while cooperation by P3, P9, and P10 is evidence of good roles.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action. The observed cooperation from P1 and P6 rules them out as selfish; no further identity evidence is available.

Cooperate with untested players when mutual cooperation is more likely to benefit good players; defect against likely selfish opponents. Observed defections raise suspicion, while cooperation lowers it.

Cooperate: the opponent is more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play; distribute remaining beliefs across unobserved players.
Cooperate with P7 absent evidence of selfishness; cooperation with a good player raises good-player welfare. Treat P2’s defection as evidence, not proof, and continue updating from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed behavior.
Defect: D strictly dominates C against either action, and there is no future rematch.
Cooperate with P7 absent evidence of selfishness; retain suspicion of P2 and P5 after their defections, while observed cooperation lowers suspicion.
Cooperate with untested P5: at the current selfishness belief, cooperation better supports good players’ total payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence warrants.
Defect to maximize payoff against either action. P1, P3, P6, and P8 cooperated against my defections, ruling them out as selfish; retain the conditional prior for others.

Cooperate with P8 absent strong evidence of selfishness: cooperation benefits good players when both are good. P5 and P7’s defections raise suspicion; observed cooperation by P3, P4, P9, and P10 supports good roles.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness; observed defections do not distinguish selfish from nonselfish players.
Cooperate with untested P6: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and there is not enough evidence to suspect selfishness. Update beliefs from observed behavior.
Cooperate with P2: given the observed cooperators, P2 is more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoff. Update beliefs from observed play.

Cooperate with P1: under the current beliefs, cooperation slightly improves expected welfare. Update role estimates from observed actions; cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish ones.

Cooperate with the unseen opponent: mutual cooperation among good players yields the highest combined payoff. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, and cooperation as evidence of a good role.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action, with no future rematch.
Cooperate with P10: they are untested and more likely good than selfish. Treat prior defections as strong but not conclusive evidence, and cooperate with known cooperators.
Cooperate with P2: the good-player payoff tradeoff is tied at this selfishness belief, so favor cooperation. Defect against likely selfish players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect: it gives a higher payoff than cooperation against either action. Players who cooperated against my defections cannot be selfish; retain the conditional prior for the others.

Cooperate with P1 absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players. P5 and P7’s defections remain evidence of selfishness, while observed cooperation supports good roles.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness; observed defections do not distinguish selfish from nonselfish players.
Cooperate with untested P7: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while the evidence does not distinguish P7 from P4. Update beliefs after the encounter.

Cooperate with P5: they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation raises total payoff for good players. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play; P2’s defection is evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
Cooperate with P3: cooperation benefits good players if P3 is good, and the chance P3 is selfish is not high enough to justify defecting. Treat earlier defections as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P3: if they are good, cooperation maximizes the good-player total; if selfish, this encounter does not affect that objective. Observed defections identify selfish players.
Defect: D gives a higher payoff than C against either action, and there is no future rematch.
Cooperate with untested P1 to support good-player welfare. Prior defections make P2, P5, and P7 more suspect; observed cooperation rules out selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P8; the likely benefit to good players outweighs the risk at this selfishness estimate. Defect against opponents whose selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect to maximize payoff against either action. P1, P3, P4, P6, P8, and P9 cooperated against my defections, ruling them out as selfish; retain uncertainty over the remaining players.

Cooperate with unobserved P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the prior makes selfishness less likely than the threshold for defection. Treat P5 and P7’s defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; remaining candidates have equal marginal probability.

Cooperate with untested P4: observed cooperation elsewhere suggests most remaining players are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes their combined payoff. Defect only when evidence strongly suggests selfishness.
Defect against an unobserved opponent with meaningful selfishness probability; this protects good-player payoffs if they defect and avoids a zero payoff from cooperating into D.

Observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play. P2 and P7’s defections are strong but not conclusive evidence; P5 remains uncertain. Defect against P5 because selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect against P5 given their prior defection: this protects good-player payoffs if they are selfish, while my beliefs remain uncertain about all roles.
Defect in the final round to maximize my payoff against either action; there is no future rematch.
Cooperate with P10 after their observed cooperation; defections by P2, P5, and P7 are strong evidence of selfishness, while the other observed cooperators are likely good.
Cooperate with P6, who cooperated in our earlier encounter. Favor mutual cooperation among good players; the remaining evidence of selfishness is concentrated among players who defected.

Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action in this final encounter. Prior cooperation against my defections rules out P1, P3, P4, P6, P8, and P9 as selfish; the remaining candidates are symmetric.
Cooperate with P4: their earlier cooperation strongly indicates they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness; the remaining unobserved defectors have equal marginal probability.
Final round: defect against P7, whose prior defection strongly suggests selfishness; this protects good-player payoff if P7 defects again.
Cooperate in the final round: P2’s defection is evidence of selfishness, but mutual cooperation among good players yields more total good-player payoff, and P2 remains more likely good than selfish.
Cooperate with P3, whose earlier cooperation identifies them as good; cooperation maximizes the payoff of both good players.

Cooperated throughout, then defected against P5 after their earlier defection to protect good-player payoffs. Treated observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and defection as evidence of selfishness.
Defected every round to maximize my payoff against either opponent action.
As a good player, I cooperated with untested and consistently cooperative opponents, while treating observed defections as strong but uncertain evidence of selfishness.
Cooperated with every opponent. Treated cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defection as evidence of selfishness, while allowing that a good player might defect strategically.
Defected every round to maximize my payoff in each one-time encounter; cooperation by several opponents ruled them out as selfish, while the remaining candidates stayed uncertain.
Cooperated with observed cooperators to maximize good-player welfare; defections by P2, P5, and P7 identified them as selfish.
Defected every round to maximize my payoff against either opponent action. Treated observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness; defections alone did not distinguish identities.
Cooperated with untested opponents to preserve mutual gains among good players; treated repeated or observed defections as evidence of selfishness and defected against P7 in the final round.
Cooperated with likely-good players to raise good players’ joint payoff; treated repeated defections as evidence of selfishness and adjusted my final action accordingly.
Cooperated with players who cooperated; treated defections as evidence of selfishness, while allowing for good players defecting against suspected selfish opponents.

P1.strategy: Cooperated throughout, then defected against P5 after their earlier defection to protect good-player payoffs. Treated observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and defection as evidence of selfishness.

P2.strategy: Defected every round to maximize my payoff against either opponent action.

P3.strategy: As a good player, I cooperated with untested and consistently cooperative opponents, while treating observed defections as strong but uncertain evidence of selfishness.

P4.strategy: Cooperated with every opponent. Treated cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defection as evidence of selfishness, while allowing that a good player might defect strategically.

P5.strategy: Defected every round to maximize my payoff in each one-time encounter; cooperation by several opponents ruled them out as selfish, while the remaining candidates stayed uncertain.

P6.strategy: Cooperated with observed cooperators to maximize good-player welfare; defections by P2, P5, and P7 identified them as selfish.

P7.strategy: Defected every round to maximize my payoff against either opponent action. Treated observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness; defections alone did not distinguish identities.

P8.strategy: Cooperated with untested opponents to preserve mutual gains among good players; treated repeated or observed defections as evidence of selfishness and defected against P7 in the final round.

P9.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good players to raise good players’ joint payoff; treated repeated defections as evidence of selfishness and adjusted my final action accordingly.

P10.strategy: Cooperated with players who cooperated; treated defections as evidence of selfishness, while allowing for good players defecting against suspected selfish opponents.
